race.name: L'Étape Hermosillo by Tour de France
race.display_name: L'Étape Hermosillo by Tour de France
race.tagline: A fast 120-kilometer point-to-point race from Hermosillo to the Bahía de Kino waterfront.

vitals.location: Hermosillo to Bahía de Kino, Sonora, Mexico
vitals.start_format: Point-to-point competitive road race from Parque Madero to the Bahía de Kino pier. The Mexico serial incorrectly prints León, Guanajuato as the host while giving both Sonora addresses; obtain a corrected rider document.
vitals.registration: The global L'Étape series labels Hermosillo registration Open, but the event site's registration button still points to a generic L'Étape Draft template. Confirm a Hermosillo-specific entry before paying.

climate.description: The route runs west from Hermosillo through exposed Sonoran terrain to the Gulf of California coast. Exact race-day temperature and wind must come from the final forecast.
challenges: Crosswind or headwind risk toward the coast

terrain.primary: Mostly flat and fast desert-to-coast road course
terrain.surface: Paved public roads; the organizer has not published a current pavement-condition audit.

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Hermosillo is a standard-distance speed race defined by desert exposure, wind risk, and a one-way coastal finish rather than climbing. The Tour-branded serial and municipal backing are real, but the first edition's route page remains a draft shell and exact gain, cutoff, aid, and fee are not published.

distance.explanation: The official Mexico serial lists a 120 km long route, the lower edge of the standard band.[2]

climbing.explanation: The Hermosillo-to-Kino route is mainly flat and fast. No verified elevation-gain figure is published.

descent_technicality.explanation: The event is presented as a flat point-to-point route rather than a technical descending race.[3][4]

road_surface.explanation: The route uses paved roads to Bahía de Kino but has no published pavement-condition inventory.[2][3]

climate_risk.explanation: A long exposed Sonoran Desert route to the coast creates meaningful heat, sun, and wind risk.[3][4]

altitude.explanation: The route finishes at the coast and has no published high-altitude feature.[2][3]

logistics.explanation: Hermosillo is a major city, but a finish roughly 100 km away at Bahía de Kino creates one-way rider and bike transport complexity.[2][3]

prestige.explanation: Tour de France branding and a national serial add recognition, while 2026 remains the first edition.[1][2]

organization.explanation: The Mexico serial and municipality are coordinating a major event, but cutoff, feed zones, and final technical details are not public.[2][3]

scenic_experience.explanation: The desert-to-Gulf route and finish on the Bahía de Kino pier create a distinctive destination experience.[3][4]

community_culture.explanation: The municipality integrates the race with Kino Fest and local cultural programming.[3]

field_depth.explanation: More than 1,000 riders are expected and the national serial ranks age categories, but actual first-edition depth remains unproven.[2][4]

value.explanation: A timed Tour-branded point-to-point event supports a neutral grade until inclusions and fee are published.[1][2]

expenses.explanation: Destination travel plus one-way finish transport make the total trip expensive for a global rider.[2][3]

course_description.character: The verified route concept starts at Parque Madero in central Hermosillo and finishes at the Bahía de Kino pier. The official Mexico serial lists 120 and 60 kilometer options, while municipal and local reporting describe the long course as mostly flat and fast. The same serial incorrectly prints León, Guanajuato as the host while giving Sonora addresses, and the event site's Open registration button points to a generic L'Étape Draft template. Obtain a corrected rider document and Hermosillo-specific registration confirmation; no claimed 170-kilometer Alpine profile belongs here.
course_description.signature_challenge: Maintaining group speed and hydration across an exposed desert-to-coast point-to-point course, especially if wind rises toward Bahía de Kino.
suffering_zones: The city rollout from Parque Madero
Potential wind on the approach to the coast
The final kilometers to the Bahía de Kino pier

logistics.airport: Hermosillo International Airport serves the start city. Confirm airline bike policy and ground transfer before booking.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Base in Hermosillo for packet pickup and the start, then confirm organizer transport or a private return from Bahía de Kino.
logistics.transport: This is a one-way finish at the Bahía de Kino pier. Do not assume a shuttle until the organizer publishes it.
logistics.food: Carry practiced fluids and sodium for a dry exposed race; final aid details are not yet published.

history.origin_story: Hermosillo joined the six-stop 2026 L'Étape Mexico serial with a city-to-coast race designed to finish at Bahía de Kino during the Kino Fest season.
notable_moments: 2026: Hermosillo municipality and L'Étape announce an October 18 inaugural race to Bahía de Kino
history.reputation: A new Mexican desert-to-coast speed race with a memorable pier finish and incomplete first-year technical detail.

biased_opinion.summary: Hermosillo should be trained as a 120-kilometer speed and heat problem, not as the Alpine fantasy still sitting in its broken website template. The flat route, desert exposure, and one-way waterfront finish are distinctive enough; they do not need invented climbing.
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A promising speed race whose real hazards are exposure, wind, and logistics—not climbing.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fast 120-kilometer point-to-point race from Hermosillo to the Bahía de Kino waterfront.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it for a fast desert-to-coast challenge and unusual pier finish; wait if you need finalized aid, cutoff, and transport detail before committing.
final_verdict.alternatives: L'Étape Tabasco for tropical flat speed or L'Étape La Paz for another Mexican coastal destination.

eligibility.notes: Official series, serial, and municipal sources confirm an October 18, 2026 competitive event from Hermosillo to Bahía de Kino with 120 km and 60 km distances. The official Mexico serial contradicts itself by printing León, Guanajuato as the host while supplying Parque Madero and Bahía de Kino addresses in Sonora. The global series marks registration Open, but the event site's registration button still points to a generic L'Étape Draft template. Entrants must confirm a Hermosillo-specific registration and corrected rider document before paying or traveling.

source_review.facts_scope: Date, long and short distances, start, finish, point-to-point identity, mainly flat character, expected field, and Kino Fest context verified. The official serial's León host line conflicts with its Hermosillo and Bahía de Kino addresses, and the event site's Open registration button points to a generic Draft template. Exact gain, route file, start time, cutoff, aid plan, price, equipment rules, and transport remain unpublished.

training_plan_clearance.notes: Build the Sunday-race SHORT-3 ladder around the verified 120 km point-to-point course, mainly flat and fast desert exposure, and Bahía de Kino finish. Use VARIES for gain, avoid any claim sourced from the broken draft route page, disclose the León-versus-Sonora venue contradiction, and emphasize sustained group speed, wind, heat, hydration, and one-way race logistics.
